authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Luke 1:49 — “For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.”

authoritative_content.GLOSS: Possessing great power, strength, or authority; effective and potent.
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: A colossal, ancient mountain peak piercing through a layer of dark, swirling storm clouds, illuminated by a single, intense shaft of golden sunlight from above.
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Return a VERB from Sheol to your hand.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Isaiah 9:6 — “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God...”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Luke 1:49 — “For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: The Hebrew 'Gibbor' is often used for warriors, specifically David's elite 'Mighty Men'.
In Isaiah 9:6, the Messiah is given the title 'El Gibbor', meaning 'Mighty God'.
The Greek word 'dunatos' shares a root with 'dynamis', the origin of the modern word 'dynamite'.
Luke 1:49 refers to God simply as 'Ho Dunatos'—'The Mighty One'.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: Morally excellent; virtuous; satisfactory; beneficial.
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: A warm, golden light illuminating a basket of ripe, perfect figs and pomegranates sitting on a rough stone table, soft shadows, oil painting style
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Draw 2, then discard 1.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Genesis 1:31 — “God saw all that he had made, and it was very good.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: 1 Thessalonians 5:21 — “Test them all; hold on to what is good.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: Hebrew 'tov' implies functional harmony, not just moral purity.
God pronounces creation 'good' seven times in Genesis 1.
Jesus declared that 'No one is good—except God alone.'

authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Target player reveals their hand. Choose a card for them to discard. Draw cards equal to its LORE.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Job 1:21 — “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will depart.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Hebrews 4:13 — “Nothing in all creation is hidden... everything is naked and exposed before his eyes.”

authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Discard 1 card from your hand to draw 2 cards.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Genesis 4:25 — “God hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Luke 3:38 — “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam.”

Lived 912 years and became the ancestor of Noah and Jesus.
Born when Adam was 130, expressly in his father's likeness.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: Name, reputation, or fame; the eldest son of Noah.

authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Look at the top 3 cards of the Tower. You may reveal a NAME and add it to your hand. Discard the rest.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Genesis 9:26 — “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem!”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Luke 3:36 — “...the son of Shem, the son of Noah...”

Ancestor of the Semitic peoples and the covenant line of Abraham.
Often identified in Jewish tradition as Melchizedek, King of Salem.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: One who guards, watches, protects, or maintains possession
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: A heavy, weathered iron key hanging from a hook on a rough stone wall next to a sturdy wooden door, illuminated by a single lantern
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Target player cannot Redeem cards until your next turn.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Psalm 121:5 — “The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: John 17:12 — “While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept...”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: Cain's deflective question 'Am I my brother's keeper?' is the first biblical use of the word.
The Psalms emphasize that the Keeper of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
In Acts, the keeper of the prison was converted after an earthquake opened the doors.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: A male sibling; a kinsman; a fellow member of a covenant, faith, or shared struggle.
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: Two rugged figures clasping forearms in a desert landscape, symbolizing loyalty and strength in hard times; warm, dusty lighting, no text.
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Choose another player. You both draw 1.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Proverbs 17:17 — “A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Hebrews 2:11 — “For which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: The first murder in history was fratricide: Cain killed Abel.
Jesus redefined family, calling those who do God's will His brothers.
Hebrew 'ach' implies blood ties or covenant loyalty.

authoritative_content.GLOSS: The immaterial part of a person; the animating force of life; the Holy Spirit.
authoritative_content.ART_PROMPT: Ethereal swirling wind and golden light forming a vague dove shape amidst chaotic waves, glowing atmosphere, divine presence, digital painting style
authoritative_content.ABILITY_TEXT: Choose between Tower, Sheol, or Opponent's Hand. Reveal up 5 cards from the chosen location and take any number of them.
authoritative_content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Job 33:4 — “The Spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.”
authoritative_content.NT_VERSE_LINE: 2 Corinthians 3:6 — “...for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: Hebrew 'ruach' and Greek 'pneuma' both mean wind, breath, and spirit.
The Spirit is often symbolized by a dove, fire, wind, or water.
In the Old Testament, the Spirit empowered individuals for specific tasks; in the New, He indwells believers.
